title: Estimating Treatment Effects in Panel Data Without Parallel Trends
abstract: arXiv:2601.08281v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for estimating treatment effects in panel data settings, addressing key limitations of the standard difference-in-differences (DID) approach. The standard approach relies on the parallel trends assumption, implicitly requiring that unobservable factors correlated with treatment assignment be unidimensional, time-invariant, and affect untreated potential outcomes in an additively separable manner. This paper introduces a more flexible framework that allows for multidimensional unobservables and non-additive separability, and provides sufficient conditions for identifying the average treatment effect on the treated. An empirical application to job displacement reveals substantially smaller long-run earnings losses compared to the standard DID approach, demonstrating the framework's ability to account for unobserved heterogeneity that manifests as differential outcome trajectories between treated and

translated_title: 无需平行趋势假设的面板数据处理效应估计
translated_abstract: 本文提出了一种在面板数据环境中估计处理效应的新方法，解决了标准双重差分（DID）方法的关键局限性。标准方法依赖于平行趋势假设，隐含地要求与处理分配相关的不可观测因素是单维的、时不变的，并以可加分离的方式影响未受处理的潜在结果。本文引入了一个更灵活的框架，允许多维不可观测因素和非可加分离性的存在，并提供了识别受处理者平均处理效应的充分条件。将该方法应用于失业（工作变动）问题的实证研究显示，与标准DID方法相比，估计出的长期收入损失要小得多，这证明了该框架能够有效解释表现为处理组与对照组之间不同结果轨迹的未观测异质性。
tldr: 本文提出了一个无需平行趋势假设的面板数据处理效应估计新框架，允许不可观测因素具有多维性和非可加分离性，并将其应用于失业研究，发现长期收入损失远小于标准DID方法的估计结果。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel framework for estimating treatment effects in panel data without the parallel trends assumption, allowing for multidimensional and non-additively separable unobservables, and finds substantially smaller long-run earnings losses from job displacement than the standard DID approach.
